Current model: flexible-total integer points

Deployed 15 October 2026 at the project owner's request as a first calibration on all 50 merged cases. Questions and expert rule connections are unchanged. The trained panel ranks raw net points directly and does not divide by a category maximum. Both panels display points, not probabilities. Explanations show actual contributions and available positive points. Bar lengths are visual aids scaled within each panel, not diagnostic percentages.

Each adjustable weight stays an integer with its original sign, within ±max(1, round(25% of its integer baseline)). Positive totals may vary from 75% to 125% of the baseline rather than being fixed at 100. The −100 exclusions remain frozen, and their categories cannot exceed 100 positive points. Zero, unobserved, and unlabeled-category rules remain frozen. No relaxed-exclusion candidate is deployed.

Training minimizes patient-balanced squared hinge loss with a ten-point margin on raw net-point differences, plus proximity penalty 0.002. Aggregate recorded-label raw points cannot fall and other-label raw points cannot rise relative to the integer baseline on training data. It uses individual one-point moves and same-sign within-category transfers for up to 30 sweeps. This is local optimization, not a global optimum guarantee.

The all-data fit has 72% patient-averaged top-three recall, 32% top-one agreement and mean recorded rank 2.91. These are training results. Eight repeated three-fold evaluations gave 66.13% top-three recall and 74.36% pairwise concordance, compared with 64.50% and 74.66% for the fixed-budget reference on identical splits. Overall predictive superiority was not established. The dataset is small, prior development used it, missing diagnoses are assumed negatives, and patient linkage is unverified. Multiple diagnoses remain possible.

Historical fixed-budget methodology and earlier results (not the current deployment)

Expert-constrained multi-label pairwise ranking scorecard

This experimental model independently supports multiple diagnoses. It does not select one exclusive class. Its percentages are normalized support scores, not calibrated probabilities. It is a constrained supervised optimizer, not deep learning, and no claim of novelty, clinical validity or journal acceptance is made.

Data assumptions and merging

At the project owner's direction, identical full question-and-answer blocks in source columns A/B are assumed to belong to the same patient. Fingerprints are computed before question filtering, including source values coerced by Excel. The 55 blocks merge into 50 assumed patients, five with two recorded diagnoses. All sheet labels are retained. Three conflicting ages are left unknown and flagged, not arbitrarily resolved. This identity assumption is not independently confirmed.

Worksheet membership supplies positive labels. Unrecorded labels are treated as assumed negatives, not clinically confirmed absences. Incomplete diagnosis recording can therefore bias training. Concussion and Neurological Other have no positive cases: their weights remain frozen and they are excluded from class-specific support evaluation, but included as comparison classes in ranking because the app displays them.

Source mappings: VMigraine → Migraine; NeuritisHypofunction → Neuritis; ScCD → Third Window; Bilateral wkns → Bilateral. The project owner explicitly confirmed NeuritisHypofunction → Neuritis. These mappings do not independently verify clinical diagnoses. Age and sex are not predictors.

Preprocessing

Revision km2-source-options-v3 (16 October 2026) keeps multiple selections for episode duration and adds structured source choices previously absent from the web questionnaire: “sneezing or blowing your nose,” “Chest pain,” and “None of the above.” These added choices have no points unless an exact scoring rule exists. Older case files with these values preserved under unscored_answers are recovered on import. The preceding duration and attack-related tinnitus revisions remain compatible.

Only existing structured questions/options are modeled. Unmatched questions/options, free text, Excel dates in choice fields and conflicting single-choice answers are omitted. Hidden conditional answers and conflicting “none of the above” selections are removed consistently with browser import. No new clinical rules are invented. Source ambiguities and missing answers require reconciliation before clinical claims.

Questionnaire revision km2-attack-tinnitus-v1 applies KM2 Sheet1!F39: question 259416 asks about unilateral roaring/ringing before or during dizziness attacks, not constant tinnitus. Explicit aliases map separate stress/anxiety and supermarket/mall/tunnel answers into the existing combined options, with each combined option counted once; a wording-only panic-option difference is also normalized. This recovered 72 option entries across 55 source blocks. Conflicting single-choice values are retained as unscored_answers in private case files. Ambiguous alternatives such as “sneezing or blowing your nose” are not inferred to mean blowing the nose alone.

New patient exports identify the questionnaire revision. In legacy JSON files without this revision, question 259416 is kept in unscored_answers rather than reinterpreted under the new wording. Reload a regenerated case file or answer that question again. No import confirmation popup is added. The original workbook is not modified.

Points and constraints

Net category points are the sum of matched signed rule weights. Support is net points divided by available positive points, clipped to 0–100%. Percentages across diagnoses do not sum to 100%. Original defaults are preserved separately.

Largest-remainder rounding creates integer baselines within each category/sign group, preserving the original rounded positive totals and negative magnitudes. Every nonzero weight keeps its sign and at least one point magnitude. Pairwise one-point transfers within the same category and sign preserve those budgets exactly. Each weight stays within ±max(1, round(25% of its integer baseline)). Explicit −100 rules, zero rules, unobserved rules and categories without positive training cases are frozen after rounding.

Objective

The current objective is pairwise learning to rank, using a squared hinge margin loss. For every patient, compare each recorded diagnosis with every unrecorded diagnosis: max(0, 0.10 − positive support + other support)². Average pairs within each patient, then average patients equally. Two recorded diagnoses are never compared against each other. The 0.10 margin is a development setting (ten support percentage points), not an established clinical separation. Support here is continuous, clipped to [0,1], before display rounding. Add 0.002 times the mean squared displacement of weights from their integer baselines, normalized by the allowed weight radius.

The previous objective independently pushed recorded support toward 1 and other support toward 0 using class-balanced squared error. That objective remains reproducible using fit(rules, records, {objective: 'support'}) and is reported alongside the ranking model. The new objective favors relative ordering rather than probability estimates. Pairwise learning to rank is an established idea; see the RankNet paper for background. This implementation is an integer scorecard with squared hinge loss, not RankNet or a neural network.

A further training-only constraint prevents macro-average recorded-positive support from falling below the integer baseline and macro-average assumed-negative support from rising above it. This constraint uses unrounded support and is aggregate, not per patient or per diagnosis. Rounding can produce tiny displayed differences. It cannot guarantee improvement on new patients.

Deterministic pairwise coordinate descent visits pairs by rule index, tries −1 then +1 point transfers, and accepts strict feasible objective improvements (tolerance 10−10). It stops after no improvement or 30 sweeps. This is a local search, not a globally optimal solution. There is no softmax, mutually exclusive label, or top-1 accuracy objective.

Evaluation and development history

The deployed weights are fitted on all 50 merged patients. Three-fold exploratory evaluation refits the model separately on each training subset. Identical modeled answer profiles are also grouped into one fold even if their full source fingerprints differ. Groups are assigned deterministically, largest first, to the fold with the smallest summed label counts, then smallest total size, then lowest index. Current folds contain 17, 17 and 16 patients. Source duplicates cannot straddle folds.

Ranking metrics report patient-averaged positive-versus-other concordance (ties receive half credit), mean recorded-diagnosis position (lower is better), whether the first displayed class is recorded, and recall of recorded diagnoses in the first three positions. Display order is rounded support, then net points, then alphabetical name, matching the app; concordance does not award alphabetical ties. These discrete metrics can differ from the continuous optimization loss. Support metrics still report macro mean support and balanced squared error. No guarantee applies to every individual patient or class. These are not calibrated probabilities or proof of clinical accuracy. The single-label prototype was superseded after discovery of cross-sheet duplicates. An initial multi-label fit raised other-diagnosis support, prompting the aggregate constraint. The ranking objective was subsequently requested to improve ordering. These are development decisions on the same cohort; results are not untouched or preregistered validation.

No independent test set exists. Small samples, assumed-negative labels, uncertain identity, source omissions and prior model development limit conclusions. See cross-validation guidance. Aggregate training and held-out metrics are retained in trained-model.js, without patient records.

Reproduction and privacy

October 14, 2026 corrected-import retraining comparison

EvaluationPairwise concordance ↑Mean recorded rank ↓Top-three recall ↑Top-one recorded ↑
Initial weights, all 50 corrected cases72.8%3.2060%36%
Support objective refit, training74.9%3.0166%38%

Both objectives above were refitted on the corrected data; the support reference is not the previously deployed model. The ranking fit has lower training top-one performance than that reference but better broader ranking. Macro recorded support is 39.31% and other support 20.38%. The aggregate constraints reference the original integer baseline. These are descriptive development comparisons, not statistically established improvements. The full-data optimizer accepted 164 one-point transfers and stopped after four improving sweeps followed by a sweep with no improvement; it did not hit the 30-sweep cap. Six of 55 recorded diagnoses remain at zero support in each model. The explicit PPPD No exclusion remains frozen at −100 per the supplied guidance; no clinical penalties were relaxed during reconciliation.

Run scripts/prepare_cohort.py on the private workbook, then scripts/train_model.cjs on its private cohort JSON. The private audit retains merged source IDs, labels, fold assignments and held-out scores. Public trained-model.js contains only weights, aggregate metrics, constraints and an extraction hash. Both browser panels use the same scoring implementation as training. Patient files stay local; drag-and-drop does not upload them. Existing single-label files are supported but should be replaced by the new multi-label patient files.

Publication requirements

Verify identities and labels, distinguish confirmed negatives from unrecorded diagnoses, resolve missing/ambiguous answers, obtain applicable research/privacy approvals, review prior art, lock an analysis protocol, and validate independently with uncertainty estimates and appropriate comparison models. This prototype and its reproducible method are not a completed publishable clinical study.
